A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Yo’City and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched, including examples relocated between the main text and appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original city-generation evaluations, GPT-5 and human comparisons, planning ablations, expansion trajectories, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5 and 10.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds CityCraft comparisons, expansion-strategy results, and a runtime/memory comparison in Tables 1, 4, and 5.

M1.justification: Appendix C changes the reported expansion encoder from BERT to Sentence-BERT. Appendix E.1 also evaluates a generator variant using FLUX.2-Klein-9B and Trellis. These are bounded component changes; the hierarchical planning procedure, refinement loop, placement objectives, and agent prompts remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100 city descriptions, prompt types, architectural domains, and city-generation/expansion tasks. The larger expansion example highlighted in v3 already appeared in v1’s appendix; the additional comparisons do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds CityCraft to Table 1 and Figures 3 and 7, retaining Trellis, Hunyuan3D, and SynCity. CityCraft also joins the efficiency comparison. New Table 4 introduces random-placement and semantics-only expansion comparators; these are targeted extensions of the comparison set.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 adds GPU-memory evaluation using FLUX.2-Klein-9B and Trellis instead of Yo’City’s generation APIs, with GPT-4o accessed through an API for all three compared methods. Expansion evaluation adds placement controls and substitutes CV for average variance. The original benchmark size, rendering protocol, and perceptual evaluation criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 and Table 4 test whether relationship-guided placement stabilizes expansion better than random or semantics-only placement. This adds a direct control experiment beyond v1’s trajectory visualization. The planning ablation, existing expansion examples, and runtime-scaling analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Expansion variability is summarized by a coefficient of variation of 3.34% instead of the previously reported average variance of 1e-4; CV is also reported for the new controls. This changes descriptive statistical reporting, without establishing additional runs. Ten human judges and twice-repeated pairwise comparisons remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Concrete evidence expands through an additional benchmark comparator, controlled expansion outcomes, and resource/quality results. CityCraft scores 0.5639 versus Yo’City’s 0.7151 in Table 1. Table 4 reports CVs of 8.76%, 5.16%, and 3.34% for random, semantics-only, and full placement. Table 5 reports Yo’City at 24.99 minutes, 24 GB, and 0.7097 VQAScore using alternative generators; this is not a same-setting performance decline. Earlier table entries and plotted curves are retained.

T1.justification: The grid formulation and distance, semantic, combined-objective, and minimization equations retain their mathematical structure. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about personalized, expandable city generation, hierarchical planning, relationship-guided expansion, and superior semantic and visual quality. The shortened conclusion and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds explanations of seam mitigation and indirect cross-grid consistency, explicitly acknowledging the absence of cross-grid interaction during 3D generation. v3 also interprets the expansion controls as evidence of robustness and discusses CityCraft’s limited applicability beyond modern-city prompts. Appendix E.2 softens observed dependence on pretrained-model capabilities into a possibility.

D1.justification: v3 specifies GPT-Image-1 where v1 used the broader GPT-Image name, revises the semantic encoder identification, and documents the FLUX.2-Klein-9B/Trellis configuration and model access information for resource evaluation. Existing hardware specifications, six agent prompts, iteration limits, acceptance threshold, and expansion weights are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Sentence-BERT, Qwen3-VL, the GPT-5 system card, and robotics/multimodal works, while removing BERT, Qwen-Image, and two fashion-generation citations. CityCraft, already cited in v1, receives explicit comparative positioning. The central contrast with SynCity and the broader research narrative remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 corrects grammar and affiliations, condenses the qualitative discussion and conclusion, adds Appendix A.3 and explanatory subheadings, and revises the efficiency discussion. These are localized edits within the retained section structure; the method narrative and agent prompts are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 3 and 7 expand to accommodate CityCraft, and Tables 4 and 5 are added. The expansion examples swap between Figures 4 and 8, while Table 3 and Figure 5 move. The revised captions introduce counting errors: Figure 4 says five expansions but shows eight, and Figure 8 says four but shows five.

improvement.justification: The CityCraft comparison, direct expansion controls, and documented resource comparison strengthen empirical support and transparency beyond v1. The benefit is limited by incomplete detail about CV aggregation and new reporting inconsistencies: expansion captions miscount steps, and Section 4.3 retains an 'at least 86%' layout-win claim despite the added CityCraft comparison showing 85.00% and 83.50%. These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the added evidence.
